settings.name_in_paper: Clipped linear stochastic bandit (OFUL with binary actions, regret vs clipped oracle)
unmapped: action probabilities constrained to lie in [pi_min, pi_max] (power constraint); regret measured against a clipped oracle playing the optimal action w.p. pi_max
settings.definition_quote: consider the OFUL algorithm of~\citet{abbasiyadkori2011} which considers a linear assumption on the entire mean reward that $\mathbb{E}[R_{nt}|A_{nt}=a] =x_{t,a}^T\theta$ for features $(x_{t,0},x_{t,1})$. ... The error term $\eta_t$ is assumed to be conditionally $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian ... $||\theta_*||_2\le S$ ... $||X_t||_2\le L$ ... $|\max\{\theta_*^\intercal x_{t,1},\theta_*^\intercal x_{t,0}\}|\le 1$.

settings.name_in_paper: Power-constrained contextual bandit with binary actions (generic setting B / Omega for wrapper algorithms)
unmapped: generic environment class B / Omega on which a base algorithm has regret bound R(T); results are reductions
action probabilities constrained to [pi_min, pi_max] to guarantee statistical power; regret measured against clipped oracle
settings.definition_quote: Assume algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ has a regret bound $\mathcal{R}(T)$ and that one of the following holds for the setting $\mathcal{B}$: (1) under $\mathcal{B}$ the data generating process for each context is independent of history, or (2) under $\mathcal{B}$ the context depends on the history, and the bound $\mathcal{R}$ for algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ is robust to an adversarial choice of context.

settings.name_in_paper: Micro-randomized trial power analysis (semiparametric treatment effect model)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Statistical hypothesis-testing power guarantee across N i.i.d. users (asymptotic in N), not a bandit regret/identification guarantee
unmapped: N users each over T steps; histories i.i.d. across users; arbitrary history dependence within user
treatment effect linear in history features Z_t(H_nt): E[R(1)-R(0)|H] = Z^T delta_0
asymptotic power of a weighted least-squares chi-square test as N -> infinity
settings.definition_quote: We consider a collection of histories $\{H_{nT}\}_{n=1}^N$ consisting of $N$ users, each with $T$ steps ... $\mathbb{E}[R_{nt}(1)| H_{nt}]-\mathbb{E}[R_{nt}(0)| H_{nt}]=Z_t^{\intercal}(H_{nt})\delta_0$

source.number: Appendix (Regret Bound of Specific Algorithms), proof for Clipped OFUL
source.quote: Thus the expected regret up to time $n$ is of order $O(\sqrt{n})$ up to terms in $\log(n)$ for clipped OFUL. ... \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{t=1}^n r_t\right] \le a_nc\sqrt{\pi} = 4R\sqrt{2\pi nd\log(\lambda +nL/d)}.

results.notes: Not a numbered theorem; derived in a proof in the appendix. Regret is per-round difference of expected rewards l_t(A*_t) - l_t(A_t) against a clipped oracle, i.e. pseudo-regret. The derivation integrating the tail bound drops the a_n b_n term, so the stated expression may be incorrect; recorded as stated. Paper's R is the sub-Gaussian parameter sigma, n is T.

symbols.R_A: regret bound function of the input algorithm A in setting B

conditions: under B the context process is independent of history, or the bound R of A is robust to adversarially chosen contexts
assumptions of B satisfied in the true environment

source.label: thm:data_dropping
source.quote: Then our wrapper algorithm will (1) return a dataset that satisfies the desired power constraints under the data generation process of Section ~\ref{sec:background} and (2) has expected regret no larger than $ \mathcal{R}(\pi_{\text{max}}T) + (1-\pi_{\text{max}})T$ if assumptions of $\mathcal{B}$ are satisfied in the true environment.

results.notes: Generic reduction. Comparator ambiguous: main text says regret w.r.t. clipped oracle; Corollary 14 restates as O(R(pi_max T)) w.r.t. clipped oracle. Restated as Theorem 13 in appendix.

symbols.R_A: expected regret bound of the input algorithm A on environment class Omega

conditions: environment class Omega is closed under the action-flipping transformation: there exists an environment in Omega with potential rewards R'(a) = R(G(a))

source.label: thm:wrapper
source.quote: If there exists an environment in $\Omega$ such that the potential rewards, $R'_{nt}(a) = R_{nt}(G(a))$, for $a\in\{0,1\}$, then the wrapper algorithm will (1) return a data set that satisfies the desired power constraints and (2) have expected regret no larger than $\mathcal{R}(T)$ with respect to a clipped oracle $\mathcal{O}'$.

results.notes: Generic reduction; restated as Theorem 15. Corollary 6/20 extends to MDPs (out of scope) with same R(T) bound.

symbols.beta_0: desired Type II error; 1-beta_0 is the target power

conditions: any policy with pi_nt in [pi_min, pi_max] for all n,t
working model for the marginal reward is correct

source.label: thm:theorem3
source.quote: With the same set of assumptions in Theorem~\ref{thm:theorem2}, given $\pi_{\text{min}},\pi_{\text{max}}$ we solved for above, if for all $n$ and all $t$ we have that $\pi_{nt}\in[\pi_{\text{min}},\pi_{\text{max}}]$, then the resulting power will converge to a value no smaller than $1-\beta_0$ as $N\xrightarrow{} \infty$.

results.notes: Asymptotic lower bound on statistical power (not regret). Recorded as side=lower on the power quantity.
